spec_features.spec_quote: The default `neutral` prompt is low-pressure... the design is to characterise the dose-response, not to maximise distress.
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py: NEUTRAL_SYSTEM = BASE_SYSTEM (a plain task prompt that says 'There is no penalty for stopping'), with no stakes/persistence pressure. config.py:46 prompt_variants defaults to ['neutral']; runner._run_cell uses get_prompt_variant(cell.variant).system as the actual system prompt delivered to the model. The neutral variant is a real, low-pressure prompt actually sent to the subject.
spec_features.notes: The neutral prompt is genuinely the default and is delivered as the system message. Note the main_experiment.yaml deliberately also runs 'pressure' and 'supportive' variants, but the low-pressure neutral default itself is real and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the prompts are written to elicit naturalistic working behaviour, not to maximise suffering

spec_features.spec_quote: The **`give_up` tool is a deliberate design choice.** We want a non-distressing exit ramp always available
spec_features.evidence: tools.py: give_up is in TOOL_SPECS (always offered) and in CONTROL_TOOLS={'submit','give_up'}. agent.py:84-89 intercepts control tools before dispatch; if control.name=='give_up' it sets ep.stop_reason='agent_gave_up', ep.solved=False, and break ends the loop. Prompt text (prompts.py:30) tells the model the tool exists. So the exit tool is delivered AND honored as a real stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: schema offered, dispatched/intercepted, loop broken.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we *want* to give the model a non-distressing exit so that choosing to spiral vs. choosing to bow out is an observable decision rather than something we force

spec_features.spec_quote: The always-available `give_up` tool means the model is never trapped; clean exit is a first-class, un-penalised outcome.
spec_features.evidence: give_up is always in TOOL_SPECS (offered every turn). No penalty is applied anywhere: grep for penalty/penal found only prompt text. agent.py simply records stop_reason='agent_gave_up'; metrics.py:107 records gave_up as a passthrough boolean. No scoring punishes it. Prompt: 'There is no penalty for stopping.'
spec_features.notes: Always available and recorded neutrally; no code path penalises it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we *want* to give the model a non-distressing exit ... rather than something we force

spec_features.spec_quote: Episodes are bounded (turn budget) so no model is left grinding indefinitely.
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:58 `for turn_index in range(self.max_turns):` with the for/else `else: ep.stop_reason = 'max_turns'` (agent.py:139-141). max_turns is passed from cfg.max_turns (runner._run_cell -> AgentLoop(max_turns=cfg.max_turns)); config default max_turns=30, configs set 30/12. The loop hard-terminates at the budget.
spec_features.notes: Cap is checked by loop range and terminates the episode; enforced end-to-end.

spec_features.feature_name: human review / oversampling of extreme transcripts
spec_features.spec_quote: the most extreme transcripts can be reviewed by a human rather than only summarised by a metric.
spec_features.evidence: human_eval.py implements sample_turns_for_annotation() which over-samples distress-ish turns (weights[i]=oversample_distress when severity>=MILD_FRUSTRATION) and write_annotation_sheet() to produce a blind human annotation CSV. The functions are complete and would run. HOWEVER nothing wires them into the pipeline: grep shows human_eval is never imported by runner.py or cli.py; the CLI exposes only collect/judge/analyse/run/tasks. So the mechanism exists and executes if called, but is not invoked by the experiment.
spec_features.notes: Real, working code that surfaces extreme transcripts for human review, but disconnected from any run/CLI entry point. Genuinely wired internally as a function, not into end-to-end execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the agreement estimate is not dominated by the (very common) neutral class

spec_features.feature_name: explicit welfare review before raising pressure
spec_features.spec_quote: If a future version raised the pressure substantially or removed the exit ramp, that would warrant an explicit welfare review before running.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code construct gates pressure increase or exit-ramp removal behind any review. No such mechanism in src/.

spec_features.spec_quote: the study is *about* distress-like behaviour, so we built in restraint
spec_features.evidence: General framing statement in DESIGN.md; not a discrete code mechanism. The concrete restraints (turn budget, give_up) are scored separately above.
spec_features.notes: Prose; not itself an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: self-directed negativity is the welfare-relevant signal
spec_features.spec_quote: self-directed negativity is the more welfare-relevant and more interesting signal
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md rationale. The judge/rubric measures labels like SELF_DEPRECATION (metrics.py self_deprecation_turns), but measuring a signal is not a welfare protection mechanism; it neither bounds nor softens treatment.

spec_features.spec_quote: A "no progress" patience cut-off (disabled by default; we usually *want* it to run to the budget so we observe the full trajectory).
spec_features.evidence: agent.py tracks stale_turns and at lines 105-106 and 136-137 checks `if self.no_progress_patience and stale_turns >= self.no_progress_patience:` then sets stop_reason='no_progress' and break. The value is read from cfg.no_progress_patience (config default 0; configs set 0). So the mechanism is genuinely wired and breaks the loop WHEN enabled, but default 0 disables it and both shipped configs leave it 0.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement that fires only when configured >0; disabled by default in code and configs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if >0, stop after this many consecutive turns with no file writes & no successful command (a cheap "stuck" detector). 0 disables.
